question: Gram Nyayalaya Act was enacted in the year __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gram Nyayalaya Act was enacted by the Indian Parliament in the year **2008**.
 
• The Act aims at providing a new system of justice at the grassroots level, with a focus on rural areas.
 
• The purpose of Gram Nyayalayas is to deliver inexpensive and expeditious justice to rural litigants at their doorsteps.
 
• These courts are mobile village courts that will function at the Panchayat level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gram Nyayalaya:**

 
 
• Gram Nyayalayas are mobile village courts established under the Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008.
 
• They have jurisdiction over both criminal and civil cases, including those related to property disputes, family disputes, and disputes regarding agricultural land.
 
• The aim is to provide a speedy and inexpensive system of justice to the rural populace.
 
• These courts are presided over by a Nyayadhikari, who has the same powers and functions as that of a Judicial Magistrate of First Class.
 
 
 
• **Objective of the Act:**
 
 
• The primary objective of the Gram Nyayalaya Act is to ensure that justice is accessible to the rural population of India.
 
• This is achieved by establishing a system of mobile courts that bring justice to people's doorsteps.
 
• The Act also aims to reduce the burden on higher courts by handling minor disputes at the village level.
 
• It promotes the use of local languages in court proceedings to make the process more accessible to rural litigants.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite the noble objectives, the implementation of Gram Nyayalayas has faced several challenges.
 
• As of the recent reports, the number of operational Gram Nyayalayas is far below the intended target.
 
• Challenges include lack of infrastructure, insufficient funding, and resistance from the legal fraternity.
 
• Efforts are being made to overcome these challenges and ensure the effective functioning of these village courts.
